title: Describing Things
summary: We learned how to describe tools and everyday objects when we don't know their name. We practised phrases like 'It's used for...' and 'It's a thing that...', the stress in compound nouns, and phrases for checking that people understand us.

grammar.title: Describing objects: It's got / It's used for / It's made of
grammar.explain: We use these phrases to describe a thing when we don't know or forget its name. After 'used for' and 'a machine for' we use the -ing form of the verb.
grammar.explain_ar: نستخدم هذه العبارات لوصف شيء عندما لا نعرف اسمه أو ننساه. بعد used for و a machine for نستخدم الفعل بصيغة ‎-ing. ونستخدم made of عندما تبقى المادة ظاهرة، و made from عندما تتحول المادة إلى شيء آخر.
form: It's got a + noun (It's got a rubber handle.)
It's used for + verb-ing (It's used for cutting wood.)
It's made of + material you can still see (It's made of plastic.)
It's made from + material that has changed (Paper is made from wood.)
It's a machine for + verb-ing (It's a machine for washing clothes.)
It's a bit like a + noun (It's a bit like a glue gun.)

examples.en: It's used for cutting electrical wires.
examples.note: used for + -ing tells us the purpose.

examples.en: It's got a little bubble in the middle.
examples.note: It's got = it has. We use it for parts of the object.

examples.en: This table is made of wood.
examples.note: You can still see the wood.

examples.en: It's a machine for shooting nails into wood.

mistakes.why: For materials we say 'made of' or 'made from', not 'made by'.
Use 'a' when you mention a part for the first time.
The wood has changed, so we use 'made from'.

quiz.q: It's used for ___ holes in walls.

quiz.why: You can still see the gold, so 'made of'.
The milk has changed into something new, so 'made from'.

quiz.q: It's ___ a safety catch, so it's not dangerous.
quiz.why: It's got = it has (a part of the object).

quiz.q: A dishwasher is a machine for ___ dishes.
It's a bit ___ a glue gun, but it melts metal.
quiz.why: 'a bit like' = a little similar to.

grammar.title: Defining relative clauses: who, which/that, where
grammar.explain: We use a relative clause to explain which person, thing or place we mean. Use 'who' for people, 'which' or 'that' for things, and 'where' for places.
grammar.explain_ar: نستخدم جملة الوصل لتوضيح أي شخص أو شيء أو مكان نقصده. نستخدم who للأشخاص، و which أو that للأشياء، و where للأماكن. لا نكرر الضمير (he / it / there) بعد أداة الوصل.
form: a person who + verb (It's a person who delivers mail.)
a thing which/that + verb (It's a thing that cuts paper.)
a thing (that) + subject + verb (It's a thing we use for cutting paper.)
a place where + subject + verb (It's a place where people live.)

examples.en: It's a guy who fixes your computer.
It's something that we use for communicating quickly.
This is the workshop where we keep our tools.
I have a friend who owns a workshop which is full of old tools.
examples.note: Two relative clauses in one sentence.

mistakes.wrong: It's a person which fixes computers.
mistakes.right: It's a person who fixes computers.

mistakes.wrong: It's a thing that it cuts wood.
mistakes.right: It's a thing that cuts wood.

mistakes.wrong: It's a place where people live there.
mistakes.right: It's a place where people live.

mistakes.wrong: It's a place which you buy tools.
mistakes.right: It's a place where you buy tools.
mistakes.why: Use 'where' for places when a subject and verb follow.

quiz.q: A carpenter is a person ___ makes things from wood.
A garage is a place ___ you keep your car.
A spirit level is a thing ___ shows if a shelf is straight.

options: It's a tool which cuts metal.
It's a tool which it cuts metal.
It's a tool who cuts metal.
quiz.why: Use 'which' for things and don't repeat 'it'.

quiz.q: A postman is someone ___ delivers mail.

grammar.title: Stress in compound nouns
grammar.explain: When two nouns go together (noun + noun), we usually stress the first word. When it is adjective + noun, we usually stress the second word.
grammar.explain_ar: عندما يجتمع اسمان معاً (اسم + اسم) نضغط عادة على الكلمة الأولى. أما في (صفة + اسم) فنضغط عادة على الكلمة الثانية.
form: noun + noun: stress the FIRST word (TEXT message, ANSWERING machine)
adjective + noun: stress the SECOND word (main BRANCH, digital CAMERA)

examples.en: TEXT message, VACUUM cleaner, LAPTOP computer
main BRANCH, mobile PHONE, digital CAMERA
It's something that we use for COMMUNICATING QUICKLY.

mistakes.why: noun + noun: stress the first word.
adjective + noun: stress the second word.

quiz.why: 'Mobile' is an adjective here, so stress the second word.

phrases.en: It's a thing that you use for...

Describing a part of an object
